title: The slot before the verb
goal: Put the new or contrasted information right before the verb, and recognize the background that speech puts after it.

intro.text: The word right before the verb is the focus: *Kitabı Ali aldı* answers **who**, *Ali kitabı dün aldı* answers **when**. In speech, known words often follow the verb: *Geldi mi Ayşe?* (has Ayşe come?). A question word never does: it is always the focus.

vocab.en: inverted sentence (with the verb not at the end)
real, actual; main (asıl sorun: the real problem)
lyrics, the words of a song (şarkı sözleri)
to collect, to compile (folk songs, texts)
by heart (ezbere bilmek: to know by heart)

exercises.question: Which sentence answers *Kitabı kim aldı?*

why.1: In this order *kitabı* stands in the focus slot. To answer **who**, put *Ali* right before the verb.
why.2: A bare object can't follow the verb, and the book is definite here: *kitabı*.
why.3: This says the book took Ali.

exercises.explain: The answer fills the slot of the question word, right before the verb: *Kitabı kim aldı? — Kitabı Ali aldı.*

exercises.prompt: It was my grandfather who collected this folk song.
accept: Dedem derledi bu türküyü.

exercises.question: *Ali kitabı dün aldı.* Which question does this sentence answer?

why.1: For **who**, *Ali* would stand right before the verb: *Kitabı Ali aldı*.
why.2: For **what**, the object would stand before the verb: *Ali dün bir kitap aldı*.
why.3: For **where from**, a place would fill the slot: *Ali kitabı dün kitapçıdan aldı*.

exercises.explain: *Dün* stands right before the verb, in the focus slot: the sentence answers **when**.

accept: It is Selin who will go to the meeting, not me.
It is Selin who is going to the meeting, not me.
It is Selin, not me, who [will go|is going] to the meeting.
Selin, not me, [will go|is going] to the meeting.
Selin [will go|is going] to the meeting, not me.
Selin is the one who [will go|is going] to the meeting, not me.
Not me, Selin [will go|is going] to the meeting.
It is not me who [will go|is going] to the meeting, it is Selin.
It is not me but Selin who [will go|is going] to the meeting.
I am not going to the meeting, Selin is.
I will not go to the meeting, Selin will.
exercises.explain: *Ben değil, Selin*: the contrasted word stands before *değil*, and the real answer, *Selin*, takes the focus slot before the verb.

exercises.prompt: Was it you who took my umbrella?
accept: Şemsiyemi sen mi aldın?
Benim şemsiyemi sen mi aldın?
(Benim) şemsiyemi siz mi aldınız?
Sen mi (benim) şemsiyemi aldın?
Siz mi (benim) şemsiyemi aldınız?
(Benim) şemsiyemi alan sen miydin?
(Benim) şemsiyemi alan siz miydiniz?

reject.why: That asks whether you took it, not whether it was **you**. Put `mI` after the word in focus: *Şemsiyemi sen mi aldın?*

exercises.explain: The focus of a yes-no question carries `mI`, and the personal ending stays on the verb: *sen mi aldın?*

exercises.question: *Gördün mü …?* Which of these can **not** follow the verb here?

why.1: A known object can follow the verb: *Gördün mü yeni komşuyu?*
why.2: A pronoun can be background too: *Gördün mü onu?*
why.3: A definite object is fine after the verb: *Gördün mü dün akşamki maçı?*

exercises.explain: Words after the verb are background. A question word is always the focus, so it stays before the verb: *Kimi gördün?*

exercises.prompt: Çok güzeldi film, ama biraz uzundu.
accept: The film was really good, but a bit long.
The film was really good, but a bit too long.
The film was really good, but a little (too) long.
The film was really good, but rather (too) long.
The film was really good, but somewhat (too) long.
The film was really nice, but [a bit|a little|rather|somewhat] (too) long.
The film was really beautiful, but [a bit|a little|rather|somewhat] (too) long.
The film was very [good|nice|beautiful], but [a bit|a little|rather|somewhat] (too) long.
The film was so [good|nice|beautiful], but [a bit|a little|rather|somewhat] (too) long.
The movie was [really|very|so] [good|nice|beautiful], but [a bit|a little|rather|somewhat] (too) long.
The [film|movie] was [really|very|so] [good|nice|beautiful], but it was [a bit|a little|rather|somewhat] (too) long.
It was a [really|very] [good|nice|beautiful] [film|movie], but (it was) [a bit|a little|rather|somewhat] (too) long.
exercises.explain: *Film* follows the verb: everyone knows which film, so the sentence opens with the reaction, *çok güzeldi*. Neutral order: *Film çok güzeldi*.

exercises.question: You are writing a report. Which sentence fits?

why.1: Verb first: fine in speech or a song, not in a report.
why.2: Inverted: the results come after the verb, as in conversation.
why.3: The time after the verb sounds like an afterthought in speech.

exercises.explain: In formal writing, keep the verb at the end. Inverted sentences belong to speech, songs and poetry.

exercises.prompt: What surprised me most was the price.
accept: Beni en çok şaşırtan fiyattı.
Beni en çok şaşırtan fiyatıydı.
Beni en çok şaşırtan şey [fiyattı|fiyatıydı].
Beni en çok [fiyat|fiyatı] şaşırttı.
En çok [fiyata|fiyatına] şaşırdım.
exercises.explain: A cleft puts the focus at the end: *Beni en çok şaşırtan* (what surprised me most) + *fiyattı*. Or keep one clause and put *fiyat* right before the verb: *Beni en çok fiyat şaşırttı*.

exercises.title: Radyoda bir söyleşi
exercises.passage:
**Sunucu:** Hasan Usta, hoş geldiniz. Bu türküyü siz mi derlediniz?

**Hasan Usta:** Hayır, ben derlemedim onu. Babam derledi, 1960'larda. Ben yalnızca plağa okudum.

**Sunucu:** Nerede duymuştu babanız bu türküyü?

**Hasan Usta:** Bir düğünde. Köyün en yaşlı kadını söylüyormuş. Babam ezgiyi hemen ezberlemiş, sözlerini de bir deftere yazmış.

**Sunucu:** Peki, sizin için asıl önemli olan ne? Ezgi mi, sözler mi?

**Hasan Usta:** Asıl önemli olan, türkünün yaşaması. Gençler de söylesin istiyorum, kendi bildikleri gibi.

**Sunucu:** Son olarak, en sevdiğiniz türkü hangisi?

**Hasan Usta:** Zor bir soru bu! Hepsini severim ben.

glossary.en: master (here: a title of respect for a musician)
to record (a song) on a record

exercises.translation: Presenter: Hasan Usta, welcome. Was it you who collected this folk song? Hasan Usta: No, I didn't collect it. My father did, in the 1960s. I only recorded it. Presenter: Where had your father heard this song? Hasan Usta: At a wedding. The oldest woman in the village was singing it, so he was told. My father learned the melody by heart on the spot and wrote the words down in a notebook. Presenter: So what really matters to you? The melody or the words? Hasan Usta: What really matters is that the folk song lives on. I want young people to sing it too, in their own way. Presenter: Finally, which is your favourite folk song? Hasan Usta: That's a hard question! I love them all.

options: The oldest woman in the village
questions.explain: *Babam derledi*: *babam* stands in the focus slot, right before the verb.

questions.q: In *Nerede duymuştu babanız bu türküyü?*, which words are background?
questions.explain: Everything after the verb is already known: the father and the song. The question word *nerede* stays before the verb.

questions.q: What matters most to Hasan Usta?
options: That the folk song lives on
questions.explain: *Asıl önemli olan, türkünün yaşaması*: a cleft puts the answer at the end.

questions.q: How does he answer the last question?
questions.explain: *Hepsini severim ben*, with *ben* after the verb: a casual, spoken order.

exercises.task: A classmate sent you this voice message. Turn it into a short written note with every verb at the end, and keep the meaning.
exercises.source: Bitti mi rapor? Ben bitirdim benim kısmımı, dün gece. Yarın gönderirim sana, sabah. Hoca istiyormuş cuma günü.
models: Raporun benim kısmını dün gece bitirdim. Yarın sabah sana gönderirim. Hoca raporu cuma günü istiyormuş. Senin kısmın bitti mi?
Dün gece raporda bana düşen kısmı bitirdim; yarın sabah sana göndereceğim. Duyduğuma göre hoca raporu cuma günü istiyormuş. Sen kendi kısmını bitirdin mi?
checklist: Every verb at the end of its sentence
Time words before the verb: *dün gece*, *yarın sabah*, *cuma günü*
The question still a question: *Senin kısmın bitti mi?*
Nothing added or left out, including the hearsay of *istiyormuş*
